corrections.source_says: Fill the measurement fields: each essay score is the mean of three independent GPT-5 evaluations; structural scales are 1-5 and holistic quality is 1-6. Diversity is dispersion of these rubric scores across essays within a condition, with VR = variance(H) / variance(H+AI) and HI = 1 - variance(H+AI) / variance(H), not an embedding-similarity measure. Record 95% bootstrap confidence intervals using 10,000 resamples and the Brown-Forsythe variance test. Human essays and their rewrites share the same source essays; no participant-level uncertainty is reported. Mention the topic-stratified robustness analyses: Perspective Plurality is approximately unchanged for Topic 0 and diversified for Topic 1, while Abstract-Concrete Oscillation reverses direction across topics.

confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion through the references and checked the cited PDF pages; the on-file document is arXiv:2603.21228v1 [cs.AI], 22 Mar 2026, 33 pages. Title and all five authors match the form (PDF p. 1; final page p. 33).

The ai_vs_human design and context class, core=no, and failure of random assignment are supported: all H+AI texts were computational single-turn rewrites, not actual student-AI interaction (PDF pp. 11-12, Section 3.3; pp. 27-28, Section 5.4).

The original dataset contained 1,378 essays: 1,375 human-written and 3 AI-generated; the latter were excluded for unknown model provenance. All five analyzed conditions have 1,375 essays, totaling 6,875 (PDF p. 10, Table 1 and Section 3.2).
The matched topic distribution is 707 essays for Topic 0 and 668 for Topic 1 in each condition (PDF p. 11, Section 3.3). These are essay counts, not verified counts of distinct students.

No randomized or analyzed people count is reported for an AI-assistance experiment; null people counts are appropriate, and the fewer-than-50-people experiment rule is inapplicable (PDF pp. 9-13, methods; pp. 27-28, limitations).

The form's 2,750 output observations per displayed two-condition contrast equal two conditions of 1,375 essays; each rewrite is matched to a source essay, so this is not a count of 2,750 independent people (PDF p. 10, Table 1; p. 15, Section 4.1).

GPT-5-mini generates or rewrites essays and GPT-5 evaluates them. Three evaluations per essay yield 20,625 API calls with no missing scores; the mean score across evaluations is analyzed (PDF pp. 11-13, Sections 3.3-3.4).
Every mean, SD, VR, confidence interval, and HI transcribed in S1-O1 through S1-O4 matches the corresponding PDF table entries (PDF p. 16, Table 5; p. 17, Table 7; p. 19, Table 8).

Every quality mean, SD, Cohen's d, and p-value in S1-O5 matches the PDF: Minimal 2.69 to 4.55, d=4.102; Structural 2.69 to 4.23, d=3.754; Delegative 2.69 to 4.74, d=4.814; all p<0.0001 (PDF p. 16, Tables 5-6).

The one-line finding's numerical claims are supported, including the rounded cohesion HI range +0.68 to +0.78, explicitly stated in the results text (PDF p. 16, Table 6; p. 17, Table 7 and Section 4.2; p. 19, Table 8).

Perspective Plurality under the Structural prompt has VR 0.959 with 95% CI [0.87, 1.07], which includes 1; the one-line finding describes its point estimate and should not be read as significant diversification under every prompt (PDF p. 17, Table 7).

This is one computational corpus study, not a synthesis, so no pooled meta-analytic estimates or study counts are applicable. No appendix or supplementary-material reference appears in the full document; generated data and code are promised upon publication (PDF pp. 9-15, methods; p. 29, Data availability; pp. 30-33, references).
summary: No randomized people study is present; this is an AI-versus-human comparison of existing essays and computational rewrites. The recorded statistics and source version match the PDF, but outcome coding, omitted outcomes, measurement details, and disclosure fields need correction.
